_comment: MVP rubric — UCS ONLY, and only signals UCS source proves outright.
No signal here may read the separate hyperswitch repo: UCS and hyperswitch are
different codebases with different connector implementations.
Every proven field below is decided by a compiler-enforced declaration:
flow  — the three-way partition in extract_flows.partition(). ConnectorServiceTrait
has no default methods, so each connector lands in exactly one of
impl / not_implemented / not_supported per flow, and the buckets
provably account for the whole fleet (asserted, not assumed).
trait — an override of an IncomingWebhook default. The defaults are inert
(Err(WebhooksNotImplemented), Ok(false)), so override-vs-default is decidable.
code  — an exact source pattern, verified arm-by-arm.
THREE OUTCOMES, NOT TWO. not_implemented and not_supported are different facts:
the generating macro documents them as 'does not yet implement' vs 'does not
support at all', and they raise different runtime errors. Only the first is work.
not_supported is reported n/a and dropped from the denominator and from effort —
charging a connector for a refund API its processor does not have would make the
backlog fiction.
TWO CONFIDENCE TIERS:
proven      — a compiler-enforced declaration or a typed field read. Every cell
is a fact. These alone determine met / gaps / effort / pct.
best-effort — a real capability with no certain signal. Shown because the
information is useful, EXCLUDED from scoring so it cannot
contaminate a number presented as provable.
A COLUMN MUST MEASURE ITS OWN LABEL. Two did not, and both are fixed:
RSync is RefundService.Get (refund STATUS), not refunding. Requiring it inside
'Refunds' marked 9 connectors that refund fine as gaps, adyen among them.
'Webhooks (payments + refunds)' never consulted process_refund_webhook and used
mode 'any', so get_event_type alone — which only classifies an event — passed.
STILL ABSENT (no honest signal at all):
Order metadata update, Smart retry — no such capability exists in UCS.
Decrypt-token / alternate-PSP      — proxy_authorize is a vault-alias proxy,
a different thing.
Relay Refund, Relay Capture        — UCS is stateless, so every refund is
already relay-shaped; the columns
duplicated Refund/Capture exactly.
Payment methods                    — source parsing is unreliable (a naive pass
classified stripe as not supporting Card)
and the field probe measures whether a
request can be BUILT, not accepted: four
permissive builders falsely probe as
supporting 103 payment methods.
Inline 3DS                         — ~28 connectors run 3DS inside Authorize
with no auth RPC. Their 3DS-artifact counts
slide smoothly 1..19 with no cliff, so any
cutoff is a knob, not a measurement.

capabilities.label: CIT
capabilities.description: Customer-initiated payment.

capabilities.label: MIT
capabilities.description: Merchant-initiated charge against a stored mandate.

capabilities.label: Manual capture
capabilities.description: Separate authorize then capture.

capabilities.label: $0 Auth
capabilities.description: Zero-amount authorization that stores a mandate.

capabilities.label: Void
capabilities.description: Cancel an authorized payment.

capabilities.label: Refunds, partial refunds
capabilities.description: Refund execution, full or partial. Deliberately does NOT require RSync: that flow is RefundService.Get ('retrieve refund status from the payment processor'), a separate capability scored in its own column. Adyen, for one, refunds fine and receives the outcome by webhook instead of polling.

capabilities.label: Refund sync
capabilities.description: Poll refund status from the processor (RefundService.Get). Independent of refunding: a connector whose processor pushes refund outcomes by webhook does not need it.

capabilities.label: External 3DS
capabilities.description: Connector accepts a 3DS result authenticated ELSEWHERE: it reads the typed AuthenticationData (eci / cavv / ds_transaction_id) off the request instead of running the challenge itself. A typed field read, so exact.

capabilities.label: Payment webhooks
capabilities.description: Handles incoming payment webhooks: overrides BOTH get_event_type and process_payment_webhook with real bodies. mode is 'all' on purpose — get_event_type only classifies an event, so on its own it processes nothing.

capabilities.label: Refund webhooks
capabilities.description: Overrides process_refund_webhook with a real body. The trait carries an inert default (Err(WebhooksNotImplemented)), so override-vs-default is decidable.

capabilities.label: NTID support for MIT
capabilities.description: Consumes a network transaction id to authorize a merchant-initiated transaction.

capabilities.label: Chargeback notification
capabilities.description: Overrides process_dispute_webhook to surface disputes.

capabilities.label: Chargeback proof submission
capabilities.description: Submits dispute evidence to the processor.

capabilities.label: 3DS (native)
capabilities.description: Connector PERFORMS the authentication itself: it implements a PreAuthenticate / Authenticate / PostAuthenticate RPC AND carries real 3DS protocol artifacts. The second condition is required because those RPCs are a generic pre/post-processing channel — flywire, grabpay, globalpay and kount use them for hosted checkout, charge-init, Confirm Transaction and risk, scoring 0-1 artifacts against 38-370 for every genuine 3DS connector. A connector that folds 3DS into Authorize with no RPC is NOT detectable this way — artifact counts across that group have no cliff, so any cutoff would be a knob rather than a measurement. Such a connector is still performing the authentication, so it is listed in `supported` once verified by hand against both its UCS source and the processor API docs. stripe is verified: it requests the challenge with payment_method_options[card][request_three_d_secure], answers requires_action with next_action.redirect_to_url, and reads the outcome from the intent.

capabilities.label: 3DS PreAuthenticate
capabilities.description: Implements the PreAuthenticate leg — 3DS version lookup and device-data collection (the 3DS Method / DDC round trip) before the authentication request. Taken from the compiler-forced flow partition, so it is exact: 17 implement, 61 declare it not_implemented, 40 not_supported. Tracked per leg rather than as a single triple because only 5 connectors implement all three, and a rollup cannot distinguish a PreAuth-only connector from a PostAuth-only one.

capabilities.label: 3DS Authenticate
capabilities.description: Implements the Authenticate leg — the AReq that returns either a frictionless result (eci / cavv / ds_trans_id) or an ACS challenge form. From the flow partition: 11 implement, 64 not_implemented, 43 not_supported. Two of the 11 (flywire, grabpay) use the RPC as a generic pre-processing channel — a hosted checkout and a charge-init — rather than for 3DS, and carry zero 3DS artifacts.

capabilities.label: 3DS PostAuthenticate
capabilities.description: Implements the PostAuthenticate leg — the post-challenge results fetch (RReq) that turns an ACS challenge into an authentication value Authorize can carry. This is the UCS flow the hyperswitch router's CompleteAuthorize leg invokes; CompleteAuthorize is not itself a UCS flow. From the flow partition: 10 implement, 66 not_implemented, 42 not_supported. Two of the 10 use it for something else (globalpay for wallet confirmation, paypal for an order-details fetch).

capabilities.label: Issuer decline code mapping
capabilities.description: The connector lifts the issuer's or card scheme's own decline code out of the processor payload into the typed `network_decline_code` field, instead of forwarding only an opaque message. Detected as a non-None write to that field, either a struct-literal value or a `let` binding consumed by shorthand init. Deliberately NOT detected from building an ErrorResponse at all (117/118 do) nor from mapping a response code to an AttemptStatus (universal status mapping, not code mapping) — both are non-discriminating. A connector that structures the decline only as a status reads as a gap here on purpose, so the 96 gaps must not be read as 'no error handling'.

capabilities.label: Merchant advice code (MAC)
capabilities.description: Surfaces the Mastercard Merchant Advice Code from a declined authorization — the code that says whether and when a recurring retry is allowed, e.g. shift4's `do_not_try_again`. Carried in the typed ErrorResponse field `network_advice_code`, so the signal is a non-None write to it. MAC here means Merchant Advice Code, not Message Authentication Code: 42 connectors use hmac, but all of it is request signing or webhook verification, which measures an auth scheme rather than a payment capability. This column measures only the feed — the GSM table, the retry decision and unified_code/unified_message do not exist anywhere in UCS source, so retryability itself is not detectable and is not claimed.

capabilities.label: Billing details
capabilities.description: The connector sends the payer's billing address or contact to the processor. Detected from a call to a billing getter on the router data (get_optional_billing, get_billing_country, get_payment_method_billing, get_shipping_or_billing_*) — a typed read of the address off resource_common_data, the only path by which billing reaches a request struct. Connector-local BillingAddress structs are deliberately NOT counted: celero, jpmorganorbital and revolut each declare one that is response-only or never constructed. Granularity is not measured — adyen sends a full address, grabpay only a country.

capabilities.label: Shipping details
capabilities.description: The connector sends a shipping address or shipping contact to the processor. Detected from a shipping getter call on the router data, excluding get_shipping_cost and get_shipping_amount_tax, which carry amounts rather than an address. Declared-but-dead fields are excluded by construction: airwallex, getnet, mollie and celero each have a shipping field assigned nothing but None, and braintree and trustpay only set the Google Pay sheet's shipping_address_required: false.

capabilities.label: L2/L3 data
capabilities.description: Level 2 / Level 3 commercial-card purchase data: purchase order number, order tax, duty and freight, discount, shipping origin and destination, and line items with commodity codes and unit of measure. UCS carries the whole bundle in one typed field, PaymentFlowData::l2_l3_data, so the signal is a read of that field off resource_common_data. Requiring the leading dot of a field access excludes the `l2_l3_data: None` test fixtures in adyen, calida and razorpay; shift4's path-spelled refusal is rejected into a provable no. Deliberately NOT counted: the generic order_details line-item path BNPL connectors use for their own order object, which is order metadata rather than commercial-card interchange data.

capabilities.label: Dynamic descriptor
capabilities.description: The connector forwards a per-payment statement descriptor that controls what the cardholder sees on their statement. UCS carries it in the typed request field billing_descriptor (whose members include statement_descriptor), so the signal is a read of request.billing_descriptor. A static descriptor configured on the merchant connector account is deliberately not counted — jpmorgan reads auth.statement_descriptor from its MCA config and even hardcodes a literal, which is not dynamic. Connector-local statement_descriptor / soft_descriptor fields pinned to None are likewise excluded.

capabilities.label: Auto capture
capabilities.description: Authorize-and-capture in one call. UCS defaults CaptureMethod to Automatic, so this is the ABSENCE of an explicit refusal rather than a positive confirmation — read a high count as 'not refused', not as 'verified'.

capabilities.label: Apple Pay — PSP decryption
capabilities.description: The connector forwards the encrypted Apple Pay token and the processor decrypts it. Detected from WalletData::ApplePay, excluding the redirect and third-party-SDK variants.

capabilities.label: Apple Pay — HS decryption
capabilities.description: The connector consumes an Apple Pay token already decrypted by HyperSwitch/UCS and sends the DPAN and cryptogram onward. This is the pre-decrypted flow: wire field apple_pay_sdk, oneof branch payment_data.decrypted_data. Detected from the domain variant ApplePayPaymentData::Decrypted and from the connector-local Decrypt*/Predecrypt* type names, since connectors spell it both ways. A connector that matches the variant only to refuse it is rejected, not counted.

capabilities.label: Apple Pay — redirect
capabilities.description: The connector hosts the Apple Pay sheet on its own page and UCS returns only a redirect. ApplePayRedirectData is an empty struct — there is no token, because the merchant holds no Apple Pay credentials on this path, so the Authorize response is a redirect rather than a charge. Detected from WalletData::ApplePayRedirect.

capabilities.label: Apple Pay — third-party SDK
capabilities.description: The processor's own mobile SDK runs the wallet flow in-app and hands back an opaque session reference; ApplePayThirdPartySdkData carries a single optional token and the connector never sees card data. Detected from WalletData::ApplePayThirdPartySdk.

capabilities.label: Google Pay — PSP decryption
capabilities.description: The connector forwards the encrypted Google Pay token and the processor decrypts it. Detected from WalletData::GooglePay, excluding the redirect and third-party-SDK variants.

capabilities.label: Google Pay — HS decryption
capabilities.description: The connector consumes a Google Pay token already decrypted by HyperSwitch/UCS. This is the pre-decrypted flow: wire field google_pay_sdk, oneof branch tokenization_data.decrypted_data. Detected from the domain variant GpayTokenizationData::Decrypted and from the connector-local Decrypt*/Predecrypt* type names, since connectors spell it both ways. A connector that matches the variant only to refuse it is rejected, not counted.

capabilities.label: Google Pay — redirect
capabilities.description: The connector hosts the Google Pay sheet on its own page and UCS returns only a redirect. GooglePayRedirectData is an empty struct — there is no token, so the Authorize response is a redirect rather than a charge. Detected from WalletData::GooglePayRedirect.

capabilities.label: Google Pay — third-party SDK
capabilities.description: The processor's own mobile SDK runs the wallet flow in-app and hands back an opaque session reference; GooglePayThirdPartySdkData carries a single optional token and the connector never sees card data. Detected from WalletData::GooglePayThirdPartySdk.

capabilities.label: AVS check
capabilities.description: The connector speaks Address Verification Service on the wire: it either sends a dedicated AVS address field or the AVS opt-in, or deserializes an AVS result off the processor response. Detected from the connector's OWN serde types — a field declaration, a serde rename to an AVS wire name, or a read of such a field — spelled either avs* or address_verification*, the two spellings the fleet uses. It cannot be a typed UCS read: UCS has no typed AVS result, the verdict travels inside the untyped CardConnectorResponse.payment_checks bag, and the one typed field that exists (request.enable_avs_check) is read by exactly one connector, worldpayraft. Note this means 'speaks AVS', not 'surfaces the verdict' — only 10 connectors populate payment_checks at all, so most yes cells read the result and drop it. stripe, revolut and worldpay are known false negatives (stripe reads both verdicts through a field named only `checks`).

capabilities.label: CVV check response
capabilities.description: The connector reads the processor's card-security-code VERDICT back off the response, as distinct from sending a CVC — almost every connector sends one, which is why the signal requires the CVV word to be followed by a verdict word (result / response / check / verification / rslt / match / reply) rather than standing alone. That one rule separates reads from sends in the same files: forte's card_verification_value, worldpayraft's card_verification_data and worldpayvantiv's card_validation_num are outbound and excluded, while cvv_result_code, cvv_check, cvv2_reply and card_validation_result are kept. Two extra arms catch spellings with no verdict word: the CyberSource-family card_verification struct, and an unmasked cvv_code (a CVC being sent is always Secret<String> under the repo's masking rule). Like AVS this is not a typed UCS read — the verdict goes into the untyped payment_checks bag under a connector-chosen key.
